items.title: Memora: A Harmonic Memory Representation Balancing Abstraction and Specificity
items.title_zh: Memora：一种平衡抽象与具体的谐波记忆表示
items.summary: Microsoft Research introduced Memora, an agentic memory framework that decouples what is stored (rich memory values) from how it is retrieved (short primary abstractions and cue anchors), plus a policy-guided retriever for multi-hop recall. It reports state-of-the-art results on LoCoMo (86.3% LLM-judge) and LongMemEval (87.4%), beating Mem0, RAG, Zep and full-context inference while using up to 98% fewer context tokens; the paper appears at ICML 2026 with code on GitHub.

items.title: SkillOpt: Agent skills as trainable parameters
items.title_zh: SkillOpt：将智能体技能作为可训练参数
items.summary: Microsoft Research's SkillOpt treats an agent's natural-language skill file as a trainable parameter outside a frozen model, running a forward–backward–update loop with a textual learning rate and validation gating to prevent prompt drift. Across six benchmarks, seven models and three execution modes it was best or tied-best in all 52 cells, raising GPT-5.5's six-benchmark average from 58.8 to 82.3 without updating any model weights; code is on GitHub.

items.title: The Log is the Agent: Event-Sourced Reactive Graphs for Auditable, Forkable Agentic Systems
items.title_zh: 日志即智能体：面向可审计、可分叉智能体系统的事件溯源反应式图
items.summary: Yohei Nakajima (BabyAGI) describes ActiveGraph, a runtime that inverts typical agent design: an append-only event log is the source of truth, the working graph is a deterministic projection of that log, and behaviors react to graph changes and emit new events with no component directly instructing another. The author argues this yields deterministic replay, cheap forking of a run at any event, and end-to-end lineage from goal to individual model call — properties retrieval-and-summarization memory lacks; an Apache-2.0 implementation is released.

items.title: Investing in multi-agent AI safety research
items.title_zh: 投资多智能体 AI 安全研究
items.summary: Google DeepMind, with Schmidt Sciences, the Cooperative AI Foundation, ARIA and Google.org, announced a technical research funding call of up to $10M focused on the safety of large-scale multi-agent systems where millions of independently built agents interact. Proposals are sought in four areas — sandboxes and testbeds, the science of agent networks, agent infrastructure, and oversight and control — with an August 8, 2026 deadline.

items.title: GPT-5.5 Codex reasoning-token clustering at 516/1034/1552 may be leading to degraded performance on complex tasks
items.title_zh: GPT-5.5 Codex 推理 token 在 516/1034/1552 处聚集，可能导致复杂任务性能下降
items.summary: A widely-discussed GitHub issue (244 points on Hacker News) reports that OpenAI Codex telemetry shows gpt-5.5 responses disproportionately terminating at exactly 516 reasoning-output tokens, with spikes near 1034 and 1552; across 390,195 response records gpt-5.5 was 19.3% of responses but 82% of exact-516 events. The reporter explicitly does not claim this proves hidden chain-of-thought truncation, framing it as a model-specific fixed-token clustering anomaly consistent with thresholded reasoning-budget behavior and asking OpenAI to investigate.

items.title: Mouse: Precision Editing Tools for AI Coding Agents
items.title_zh: Mouse：面向 AI 编程智能体的精确编辑工具
items.summary: HIC AI's Mouse is a file-editing tool for AI coding agents that replaces plain string-replacement with six declarative coordinate-based operations (INSERT, DELETE, ADJUST, etc.), staged changes with atomic rollback, and 'tool-response engineering' that embeds contextual guidance and risk assessment in every tool response. It ships as a VS Code / Open VSX extension.

items.title: Securing the future of AI agents
items.title_zh: 保障 AI 智能体的未来安全
items.summary: Google DeepMind detailed its AI Control Roadmap, a defense-in-depth framework that treats internal agents as potential insider threats and layers system-level security on top of model alignment, using trusted AI 'supervisors' to monitor an agent's reasoning and actions. The team says it has already analyzed a million coding-agent trajectories, noting most flagged events stem from agent misinterpretation or overeagerness rather than adversarial intent, and published a companion policy paper, 'Three Layers of Agent Security.'

items.title: LLMs are stuck in a groupthink groove. This startup is trying to get them out.
items.title_zh: 大语言模型陷入了“群体思维”的窠臼，这家初创公司正试图让它们摆脱
items.summary: MIT Technology Review reports on Australian startup Springboards, whose model Flint — built on Alibaba's open-source Qwen 3 — is trained to inject variety only at specific output points rather than raising temperature globally, addressing the tendency of mainstream LLMs to converge on homogeneous answers. It cites the NeurIPS 2025 best-paper 'Artificial Hivemind' study, which found 25 different LLMs largely converged when asked open-ended questions.

items.title: Unlocking UK house-building with AI-accelerated planning
items.title_zh: 以 AI 加速规划审批，助力英国住房建设
items.summary: Google DeepMind is partnering with the UK government, Google Cloud, Faculty and councils in Barnet, Camden and Dorset on a Gemini-based prototype that assists planning officers by consolidating data, identifying relevant policies with citations, summarizing feedback and drafting assessments, aiming to cut householder application decision times by 50%. The officer remains the final decision-maker with a recorded chain of thought and audit trail, and the government plans national availability from 2027.
